title: Jumpr <> Wagertech: Project Kickoff

items.topic: GitHub repository access for team member
items.statement: Jess said he will add a person (not named in the transcript) to the GitHub repository right after the call.
items.quote: Jess Hodgson: I'll get I'll get him added to that GitHub thing right after this call.

items.topic: Rough three-phase timeline estimate
items.statement: Waleed gave a rough estimate: Phase 1 (sign-ups) by mid-August, the second phase (he said payouts) about one more month, and Phase 3 another month to month and a half. He cautioned against treating this as a firm completion date.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So we've like outlined three phases. The first phase kind of getting you signups um in by mid August. / Waleed Alasadi: The second phase with like payouts um and and that kind of component. We pro probably another month on top of that. another month to month and a half on phase three.

items.topic: Change management and adoption risk
items.statement: Waleed flagged change management as a risk: Salesforce integrates with the WagerTech API and changes how at least 23 people work, and users find spreadsheets easy today. Jess agreed that client-side delays and slow adoption can extend the timeline.
items.quote: You're changing at least 23 people how they work. / So there is definitely a change management component that we have to consider when we're thinking about what does done really

items.topic: November 1 rough efficiency-measurement date
items.statement: Jess proposed November 1 as a high-level planning date to start measuring efficiencies (end of October for Phase 3), not counting client-side delays or slow adoption. Waleed agreed this was fair as a rough estimate.
items.quote: Jess Hodgson: one. So um I'm sure that that that's all I'm trying to do is build a business plan around some of the measurable sides of things. So look, I think you made it pretty clear it's mid August phase one, mid, we'll call it end of October phase three and so November 1st / Waleed Alasadi: So that that is that is absolutely fair to say.

items.topic: Firm up timeline after discovery
items.statement: Jumpr will come back with a more confident timeline after 1.5 to 2 weeks of discovery and solution design. Jess set the second week of July to confirm or amend the November 1 estimate; Waleed agreed and hoped for earlier.
items.quote: Jess Hodgson: We'll set a a very rough estimate of November 1st and we'll solidify that or at least have a lot more certainty around that particular date or if it's going to be amended in any capacity by the second week of July. / Waleed Alasadi: That's fair to say.

items.topic: In-person project plan meetup in Toronto
items.statement: Joyce suggested an in-person meetup in Toronto (WagerTech is there the week of July 8-9) to talk through the detailed project plan. Jess and Waleed agreed. Jess said to put it in the calendar for the second week of July. The transcript does not show that a specific date or time was booked.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So, it would be kind of cool to have like an in-person meetup to talk through what you're describing around like the more detailed project plan. / Jess Hodgson: Yeah, let's show you book a lunch or something. / put in the calendar, second week of July, do it in person

items.topic: Emily is WagerTech PM and primary contact
items.statement: Emily (Director of Operations) confirmed she will manage the project on the WagerTech side and be the primary point of contact for Jumpr questions. She will not work in the Salesforce back end.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I will not be on the back end. / Joyce Kiddell: is it fair to say like you're essentially the project manager and primary point of contact like if they have questions? / Emily Vandenberg: Yes, / Emily Vandenberg: absolutely.

items.topic: Lina signs off on major milestones
items.statement: Lina (COO) said her role is key stakeholder who signs off on major milestones and guides operations and process decisions.
items.quote: But my my role for the Salesforce implementation I think is just maintaining like as a key stakeholder signing off on major milestones

items.topic: Live, clean data; reps sell not admin
items.statement: Lina said WagerTech wants live, clean data. Brand ambassadors enter data themselves today and are not reliable at it. A goal is for reps to sell and spend less time in Google Sheets.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Yeah. Like we we want live data. / Lina Ceniccola: We want it to be a clean as well. We rely on our brand ambassadors to input the data themselves which is not the most they're not the most reliable to start with / one of the goals of the project is again to actually drive them to sell and spend less time in Google Sheets

items.topic: Joyce to update PRD in Notion
items.statement: Joyce said some areas were fleshed out or added since the PRD was sent. Kobi asked for the updated version. Joyce will update the PRD in Notion within about a day and message Kobi when done.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I will say though that there are a couple areas that we've even further fleshed out or added to the plan that isn't present in the parody since we sent it over. / Joyce Kiddell: So, um, I'll update it. Just give me like a day and I'll I'll just shoot you a message when it's the most update version in

items.topic: Straw's operator data warehouse workstream
items.statement: Strahinja is working on a data warehousing project: third-party data from operators (casinos), not entered by users, goes into a data store that may link to Salesforce, to validate what sales reps record.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: I'll be working on a project to move that into a manageable data / Strahinja Vladetic: store that we can then link up to Salesforce hopefully. / Strahinja Vladetic: Uh these would be like third-party data from the other from the operators that they work with. / Strahinja Vladetic: So the casinos um to validate the the stuff being recorded by

items.topic: Centralize in Salesforce, retire spreadsheets
items.statement: The project goal is to bring everything into Salesforce as one central system and retire the Google spreadsheets. Lina said retiring Google Sheets is what she is most excited about.
items.quote: Um, and what I'm most excited about is to retire Google Sheets. / our goal for this project is to bring everything uh into a centralized system which is going to be Salesforce. Uh we are going to retire all those Google spreadsheets.

items.topic: Dropbox/uploads storage options and recommendation
items.statement: Kobi said the Dropbox and upload handling needs more discussion, with low cost in mind. Jumpr will look at the options and come back with recommendations; this could be a temporary solution first and a better one later.
items.quote: the Dropbox, the the uploads, uh those we're going to have to have some conversations around the best way forward. Um because obviously you want to keep the cost low as well. / We'll do a deeper dive into what our options are and get back to you with uh with recommendations and we can pick whatever whatever works for you, whether it's like, you know, a temporary solution for now and then a better solution later on.

items.feature_area: Sign-Up (incl. study link click / SLC intake, sign-up proofs, fraud flags, sign-up list view)
items.topic: Single-entry sign-up logging with fraud flags
items.statement: Kobi described rep interfaces to log sign-ups more easily, with fraudulent users flagged up front, and one point of entry instead of entering data in several places.
items.quote: that does mean we're going to be able to set up interfaces for your reps to uh log their signups uh in a much easier way with a way to flag those fraudulent uh users up front. / there might still be data entry, but it's one point of entry that's going to log everything that they need to log in one go.

items.topic: Real-time reporting on sign-ups, referrals, players
items.statement: Kobi said data in Salesforce will support real-time reporting on sign-up volumes, utilization rates, referral counts and player counts. Report details are to be worked out during design.
items.quote: You're going to be able to see those signup volumes, um the utilization rates, um the number of referrals that are coming in, uh number of players, all of those things in real time.

items.topic: Native-first build, flows over Apex
items.statement: Kobi said Jumpr will keep the build simple and as native as possible, preferring flows over Apex and adding customization only if really needed, so any Salesforce admin can maintain it.
items.quote: Keep it as native as possible, meaning like we make use of Salesforce functionality as much as possible. We're not going to dive right into customizations or Apex, uh, right away. / prefer flows over Apex is any Salesforce admin can manage it.

items.topic: Holistic data model design in Phase 1
items.statement: Phase 1 includes solution design and data architecture for the whole project, including payouts and deposits. Jumpr might build later-phase objects now for relationships, with their automations and interfaces coming in later phases. This is to be planned after discovery.
items.quote: what we're going to get done within this phase is the solution design and data architecture um this is you know finalizing the data model um not just for what we're releasing for this phase but also for like the payouts the deposits and everything / we might, you know, build those objects that we need for later phases now. Um just so yeah, the relationships and stuff, but the automations, the interfaces and everything that we might need to build for those later uh later uh objects might just come in those later phases.

items.topic: Phase 1 core data model components
items.statement: Kobi listed Phase 1 core data model work: attribution, deal tracking, and intake and lead-to-player conversion (sign-up forms and API endpoints). Jumpr needs to review the sign-up forms and API endpoints that week. He said everything is negotiable.
items.quote: we're going to set up the attribution, um the deal tracking, um the intake and lead to player conversion. Um this is where your signup forms and API endpoints come into play. Um so we will need to dig into those um probably not today, but it sometime this week.

items.feature_area: Sign-Up (incl. study link click / SLC intake, sign-up proofs, fraud flags, sign-up list view)
items.topic: Sign-up logging UX, fraud flags day one
items.statement: Kobi called the sign-up logging experience the most important part of the project for rep adoption. He said fraud flags and exception handling are also part of day one, and that the PRD is about 80% there.
items.quote: the signup logging experience. I think that's probably going to be the most important part of this project because that's what we need to make sure it's easy enough for the reps to use on a day-to-day basis so that adoption is there. / Fart flags, exception handling, um, these are all also part of day one.

items.topic: PRD phase breakdown: deposits P2, payouts P3
items.statement: Kobi restated the PRD phases: Phase 1 foundation and sign-ups; Phase 2 deposits, caps and bank transfer tracking; Phase 3 payouts and reporting. These could change after discovery. This differs from Waleed's earlier remark that the second phase covers payouts.
items.quote: we have the phase one which is a foundation and signups. / Um and then phase two deposits, caps, uh bank, uh bank transfer tracking, um and then payouts and reporting in phase three.

items.topic: Build everything in a sandbox
items.statement: Joyce asked about a test environment. Kobi confirmed Jumpr will build everything in a sandbox, because auto-generated IDs and number fields would start counting in production. Joyce accepted.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So I I'm going to mention that in the next step but we are going to build everything in sandbox. / Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah, the reason for that is um there are certain fields like autogenerated ids and number fields that are going to start the moment we start adding records. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah.

items.topic: Iterative testing plus end-to-end test guideline
items.statement: WagerTech will test components during the build in weekly cycles, followed by full end-to-end testing near the end. Kobi will provide the sandbox and a guideline of what to test.
items.quote: you are going to test throughout the build. / Um and then uh we'll have like a full end to end testing near the end. We'll provide you the sandbox and I usually like to also provide like a guideline of what to test, what to look out for at least from our end. / Joyce Kiddell: Perfect.

items.topic: Reuse WagerTech ERD, propose changes
items.statement: Joyce asked whether Jumpr would make a separate data model document. Kobi said he will not rebuild from scratch: the existing ERD is 80-90% there. He will propose some changes (for example master-detail vs lookup) for agreement and does not expect major changes. Joyce accepted.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um I'm not going to try to rebuild everything from scratch. I think you're like like I said, you're like 80 90% there. Um, there are some some things off the top of my head that I think we should do differently, but I'm going to propose it. / Joyce Kiddell: Perfect.

items.topic: Historical data migration in Phase 1 for go-live objects
items.statement: Joyce asked to include historical data migration, for example sign-up data in Phase 1 and redeposits and payout tracking later. Kobi confirmed data migration is in Phase 1, at least for the objects that go live.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, so maybe like knowing we're doing process flows in phases, like if we could potentially import all of our signup related data in phase one and then do the same for like redeposits and uh payout tracking in the later phases. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So I did include data migration in this phase um at least for the objects that we go live with. / Joyce Kiddell: Okay.

items.topic: Possibly load later-phase object data early
items.statement: Kobi said that if later-phase tables (for example payout objects) are built in Phase 1 for relationships, Jumpr could also load that data, even without automations or validation rules.
items.quote: even if those uh those other objects from later phases don't have the automations or validation rules or anything supporting it um as long as the table spin up we could upload that data too

items.topic: Return Salesforce unique IDs to legacy trackers
items.statement: Waleed said Phase 1 will create the entities (players, operators such as BetMGM) with unique IDs. Jumpr could work with WagerTech to take those IDs back into the existing tracking systems so later data loads do not need remapping.
items.quote: for sure in phase one is the entities are going to be created. So the players will be created the bet MGMs will be created. um those will generate a unique ID and we probably can work with your team to take that unique ID back to your existing tracking systems

items.topic: Payout data may need transformation before import
items.statement: Waleed warned that payouts (from the Airtable work) may need more objects (helper, rollup, payout lines), so data may need transforming before import. Payout line design may not be known until Phase 2. Data imported early would also need to be kept up to date.
items.quote: I think that you may be like still missing some objects like you're saying like helper objects, rollup objects, there's going to be sometimes like when we talked about payouts, maybe line items. Um so there might be need a transformation of the data before we um actually preload it right. / we may not necessarily know exactly how payout lines will work until like I don't know phase two and may maybe not.

items.topic: Payouts modeled with payout lines
items.statement: Waleed said the plan is to model payouts with payout lines, but how payout lines work is still unknown.
items.quote: payouts we do want to do payouts with payout lines.

items.topic: WagerTech transforms data; Jumpr imports
items.statement: Joyce said WagerTech can do the data transformation if Jumpr says what is needed. Jumpr would do the import and make sure the data fits the structure. Waleed agreed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: we can actually handle the data transformation on our end. Um, and then you guys would just have to worry about like doing the import and making sure like everything lands within the structure you set / Waleed Alasadi: Yeah. No, for sure.

items.topic: Iterative delivery, internal UAT, one-week UAT
items.statement: Kobi described the delivery approach: iterative build with two-week cycles, demos as components are ready, Jumpr internal UAT, about a week of client UAT, then go-live deployment, training and post-go-live support.
items.quote: Um, I'm going to do like two week uh sprint cycles, but we don't really do like thick sprints. / Um we also do our own internal UAT / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um and then we'll usually do like a week or so of UAT. Um and then once we're all good, we'll start planning for the go live production deployment training. Um and then post go live support.

items.topic: Asana for user stories, tasks and updates
items.statement: Joyce asked whether Asana would hold release notes. Kobi confirmed user stories, tasks and updates will be in Asana, with story-specific communication kept in the Asana tickets.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So is is sauna where we would have like release notes essentially. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh yeah yeah yeah like user stories um uh all the all the cards all the tasks um and updates will be through Asana.

items.topic: Set up Slack channel
items.statement: Kobi will set up a Slack channel for day-to-day communication and add everyone to it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um but you're also going to have access to a Slack channel where you can communicate with us on a daily basis. / I'll set up that Slack channel and uh add you all to it as well.

items.topic: Train-the-trainer approach
items.statement: Kobi said Jumpr usually uses train-the-trainer: train a few WagerTech staff who then train the wider team. Sessions will be recorded. Jumpr can also train end users if WagerTech wants. Not confirmed.
items.quote: Typically, we go with a train the trainer approach um where we train a few of you and then you train the larger team. / but if you want us to do the training to your end users too, happy to do that as

items.topic: Training and go-live at end of Phase 1
items.statement: Joyce asked whether training and go-live are for all of Phase 1 or for each two-week release. Kobi said they come near the end of Phase 1, once data migration is done and users can move off the spreadsheets. Demos and testing happen during the build.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: like that's for the entire phase one, right? Or are you talking about like the chunks of twoe releases? / the data migration needs to be done and they could be basically moving off of the spreadsheets and into Salesforce. So it is going to be closer to the end.

items.topic: Involve end users early in demos
items.statement: Kobi invited WagerTech to bring end users into demos and testing from the start so they know the system before UAT.
items.quote: Um and feel free to bring in users, right? / it's always nice to have end users uh come in and start uh chipping in from the beginning.

items.topic: Connect Salesforce to redeposit/payout sheets
items.statement: Joyce said work is needed at the end of Phase 1 to connect Salesforce to the redeposit and payout tracking spreadsheets, because users will still use the redeposit flow and sheets while redeposits are built. Kobi parked it for a discovery session.
items.quote: there has to be a little um work accounted for at the end of phase one to connect Salesforce into the other spreadsheets for like redeposits and payout tracking to ensure that like there's still some form of connectivity between the two systems. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we need to double click on this during like one of our discovery meetings and see what that looks

items.topic: Keep systems connected until all flows live
items.statement: Joyce and Lina said the sign-up, redeposit and referral sheets are linked. Salesforce sign-ups must keep feeding the redeposit and referral tracking until all flows are live, because referrals and redeposits depend on sign-ups.
items.quote: we kind of have to like make sure that Salesforce signups are talking to redeposits. / Lina Ceniccola: We just want our system to stay connected until all flows are / Lina Ceniccola: because the other two flows are reliant on the sign up flow. Like you don't have a referral without a signup.

items.topic: Google Sheets plugin to sync sign-ups
items.statement: Waleed suggested a Google Sheets plugin or a Salesforce sign-up report that syncs to the sign-up sheet (for example once a day), so other sheets keep working off it. Users would do sign-ups in Salesforce and the rest in the sheets. The plugin is to be chosen later; more discussion in discovery.
items.quote: I've worked with like for example a lot of Google um like plugins with Google Sheets and what it can do is it can pull the player signups that happen in Salesforce like right into like each like each Google sheet. / Yeah, we could talk about that more in discovery. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, that's that sounds like basically all we'd / the signup sheet. Um, either like once a day, every once often. There's so many plugins like we can see which one works the most sense for

items.topic: Pull redeposit/referral inputs into Phase 1?
items.statement: Kobi said that after discovery they should check whether some redeposit and referral input points should come into Salesforce from the start, and adjust timelines. He said it is too early to tell.
items.quote: if it makes sense to pull some of those things into Salesforce from the beginning without obviously like any thirdparty integrations or anything like that um and kind of readjust the timelines. But again, after discovery, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think it's too early to tell.

items.topic: Keep phased rollout, early first milestone
items.statement: Waleed said WagerTech wants a first milestone as soon as possible to get usage, then add more. Each sheet stands alone, so redeposits cannot be partly migrated. Kobi agreed that phasing also stops reps from being overwhelmed.
items.quote: the team at Wagert Tech has indicated that they are looking to kind of have that first like milestone as soon as they can um get some usage, get the feel of Salesforce and then add on more on top, right? / so like I don't think we can like migrate portion of redeposits but not like the whole / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, that's fair. It's also like if we don't phase it, it's a lot for reps to learn from day one

items.topic: Shared Google Drive for recordings and docs
items.statement: Jumpr will set up a shared Google Drive for meeting recordings, documents and deliverables that everyone on the project can access.
items.quote: we'll also set up a shared Google Drive to dump like meeting recordings like this one.

items.topic: Weekly sync scheduling
items.statement: Weekly syncs start next week at 30 minutes, growing to an hour later for demos. Kobi will send a scheduling link and coordinate after the call.
items.quote: Uh we'll start the first one next week. / We'll start with like 30 minutes for now and then as we get deeper into the project, this will probably extend into like an hour block / I'll send out a link for scheduling the weekly uh weekly sync.

items.topic: Jumpr response-time SLA
items.statement: Kobi stated Jumpr's response time: non-urgent items in one to two business days, urgent items within one day. He said they are usually close to real time on Slack.
items.quote: generally anything not urgent, it's like one to two business days and uh if it's urgent within within one day.

items.topic: Add attendees to Asana board
items.statement: Kobi will add all attendees to the Asana board after the call.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um and I will add all of you to the board uh after the call as well.

items.topic: Tentative Phase 1 go-live August 17
items.statement: Kobi set August 17 as a tentative Phase 1 go-live date and planned backward from it. Go-live comes after build, UAT, client sign-off and training.
items.quote: So I picked like the first Monday in mid August, August 17 as a tentative go live date.

items.topic: Reporting and dashboards after go-live
items.statement: Kobi said reporting and dashboards usually start after go-live, because data is needed first (from user activity and data migration).
items.quote: usually after go live is when we start doing the reporting and dashboards um because we need data in there, right? / So we'll do the reporting and dashboards in that phase

items.topic: One-week UAT and sign-off before go-live
items.statement: Kobi allowed about one week for UAT in the week before go-live, with UAT sign-off hoped for that week and everything ready for UAT the week before. UAT can be extended if needed.
items.quote: specifically the week before um I'm bucketing about a week for UAT. um if we need longer um after you know we build everything we can adjust the timelines / Uh the week before, uh we're hoping for sign off on the UAT. Um so the week before that we'll have everything ready for UAT.

items.topic: Trial data migration in sandbox first
items.statement: Kobi usually does a sandbox migration first to find data errors before the production import. This may happen earlier if time permits and the data is complex.
items.quote: usually I like to do like a sandbox deploy uh sandbox migration first just to test the data to see if there's any errors before we do it in production. / So if time permits and if the data is very complicated then we might do that um earlier on

items.topic: Discovery inputs expected by next Wednesday
items.statement: Kobi expects to have all the information Jumpr needs by next Wednesday. After discovery he will break the work into user stories and map the build order.
items.quote: once we do the discovery and break down the user story, I'll kind of map it out based on what we're going to work uh in what logical order. / I'm expecting that by next Wednesday we should have all the information that we need, if not sooner.

items.topic: Five-week build; early finish options
items.statement: Kobi said the build has five weeks and might finish sooner if it sticks to the PRD scope. If so, WagerTech can choose to wait until mid-August, ship early, or bring later phases forward.
items.quote: we have five weeks and I think it's a lot of time. / And if we get it done sooner, then I'll leave it up to you if you want to still wait until uh like mid August or if we want to ship earlier or if we want to move later phases up ahead.

items.topic: Timeline optimism not aligned within Jumpr
items.statement: Waleed said openly that he is less optimistic than Kobi about the timeline for turning the workflows into a good user experience, and that it is too early to discuss the timeline.
items.quote: like Kobe's optimism about the timeline is different than mine on like actually translating the workflows to like usable user like I don't know user forward / anyway it's too early to talk about the timeline but Like that's somewhere where maybe we're not necessarily super

items.topic: Set up sandbox this week
items.statement: Jumpr will set up a sandbox this week so work in Salesforce can start.
items.quote: this week we'll get a sandbox set up. Um, so we can start working in the uh in Salesforce.

items.feature_area: CMS Integration (SF→CMS and CMS→SF webhooks/API, payloads, external IDs)
items.topic: Extra discovery session on API integration
items.statement: Only one discovery session is booked. Kobi said at least one more is needed for the API integration and the technical setup already in Salesforce, and Jumpr will set it up.
items.quote: I think we are going to need at least one more to dive into the API uh integration and uh and like the technical implementation uh of what's already in Salesforce. / we'll set up a another discovery call to dive into what this looks like, what you already have set up.

items.topic: Follow-up ERD deep dive
items.statement: Emily said a deeper ERD session will not happen today and a follow-up should be planned. Kobi said it is not urgent and he will set up a call if he has specific questions after learning the process.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I think you were talking about wanting to go kind of deeper on the erd as well and I know we said we would save time but probably won't get there today so we should just account for a / Kobi Kunasekaran: Sure. Yeah. And I I think it doesn't need to be urgent either. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um I think like once we understand the process we can if I have like specific questions um yeah we can reach out and set up another call.

items.topic: Salesforce access and license provided
items.statement: Kobi confirmed WagerTech has already given Jumpr Salesforce access and a license.
items.quote: generally we need access to Salesforce and the license. You've already given us that.

items.topic: WagerTech reps available for UAT
items.statement: Kobi asked WagerTech to have a few reps set aside time for UAT in the last week of July or first week of August, and ideally to give early feedback during the build.
items.quote: at the very least during that last week in or first week in August when we go into UAT, you want to make sure you have a few uh few reps available to uh test it, you know, set aside that time to go through that.
items.due: last week of July / first week of August

items.topic: WagerTech time needed during discovery
items.statement: Kobi said Jumpr needs time from WagerTech teams for the next one to two weeks of discovery to finalize the design.
items.quote: for this next week, I'm going to say maybe two weeks actually. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um we are going to need time from your teams um during discovery as we have questions as we form the as we finalize the design.

items.topic: Spreadsheet templates for historical data prep
items.statement: Once the data model and approach are set, Kobi will create spreadsheet templates for WagerTech to fill in with historical data. He expects them around mid-July.
items.quote: I I can set up some uh Google uh sorry spreadsheet templates for you to start filling out and uh we you can start putting the data together. Um probably won't have this until probably midway through July.

items.topic: Separate data store integration with Salesforce
items.statement: Strahinja asked for a chat about WagerTech's separate data store, which may pull data from Salesforce and in some cases push to it. He wants to confirm the chosen store will not get in Jumpr's way. Kobi suggested covering it in the ERD walkthrough.
items.quote: Strahinja Vladetic: So, we're going to have a data store that's separate from Salesforce that potentially needs to pull in data from Salesforce and maybe in some cases push. / Strahinja Vladetic: I just wanted to confirm with you guys that that won't get in your way or that it sounds like the right decision. Just tentatively out there. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, maybe when we set up the time for the erd walk through, we can go through that as well.

items.topic: Tell Jumpr about ongoing Salesforce work
items.statement: Kobi assumes the build is more or less from scratch. He asked WagerTech to tell him about anyone currently working on Salesforce, so Jumpr can coordinate and not wipe their work.
items.quote: I'm assuming we're more or less starting from scratch and we're building everything from scratch. But if there is any ongoing work, anybody working on any uh any component whether it's like part of this project or other projects, let me know so that we're not stepping on toe and we can coordinate uh and work together.

items.topic: WagerTech admin joins after discovery
items.statement: WagerTech will bring its Salesforce administrator (who will take over from Jumpr) in after discovery, not now; the person is still being decided internally. Waleed asked why not now. Emily and Joyce said this was intentional, to keep this round to the main business stakeholders. Waleed accepted.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, I think we're still talking internally about like who exactly. / Joyce Kiddell: Um, but the plan would be once we get past discovery, um, we would want to bring in that person to kind of ride along through the process. / Emily Vandenberg: We wanted to keep it to the main like business kind of like stakeholders in this in this round. / Waleed Alasadi: That's totally fair.

items.topic: Review existing Salesforce setup and custom UIs
items.statement: Kobi wants to go through the current Salesforce setup, including the custom-built UIs, to learn what did not work for the business and avoid repeating it. Emily agreed and said she will probably set up a separate call.
items.quote: like talk through what uh what's been currently set up and what was the thinking behind it and uh why it is set up that way. like there are like some interesting UIs that were like custom built in there. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, fair and valid. And we can defin I'll probably just pull it into another um call if we can't get to it.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Timeline for Salesforce Integration: ... Waleed Alasadi outlined a three-phase structure: Phase 1 (signups) by mid-August, Phase 2 (payouts) approximately one month later, and Phase 3 (final components) ...
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... Um and then phase two deposits, caps, uh bank, uh bank transfer tracking, um and then payouts and reporting in phase three.
gemini_disagreements.why: The Gemini Details section puts payouts in Phase 2, following Waleed's informal remark (line 166). Kobi's PRD-based breakdown puts payouts in Phase 3 and deposits/caps/bank transfers in Phase 2. The transcript itself is inconsistent; Gemini shows only one version and does not flag the conflict.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: In-person team project meeting scheduled An in-person team meetup is scheduled for the week of July 8th in Toronto to conduct a detailed review of the project plan.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Jess Hodgson: Yeah, let's show you book a lunch or something. ... put in the calendar, second week of July, do it in person
gemini_disagreements.why: Gemini Decisions says the meetup is 'scheduled'. The transcript shows agreement to plan it, but no booked date or time; Gemini's own Next steps calls it an item still to 'coordinate'. The summary is firmer than the transcript.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [Kobi Kunasekaran] Schedule discovery meeting: Schedule a follow up discovery meeting to discuss API integration, technical implementation details, and the entity relationship diagram walkthrough.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Sure. Yeah. And I I think it doesn't need to be urgent either. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um I think like once we understand the process we can if I have like specific questions um yeah we can reach out and set up another call.
gemini_disagreements.why: The API discovery session was firm (line 664). Kobi made the ERD walkthrough conditional and not urgent ('if I have like specific questions'), and later said only 'maybe when we set up the time for the erd walk through' (line 716). Gemini puts the ERD walkthrough into a firm scheduling action.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Coordination of Salesforce Development: ... Kobi Kunasekaran emphasizes the importance of collaborating rather than wiping out active components, as the team intends to build from scratch while ensuring no prior work is compromised.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... I'm assuming we're more or less starting from scratch and we're building everything from scratch. But if there is any ongoing work, ... let me know
gemini_disagreements.why: Kobi stated an assumption ('I'm assuming ... more or less'). Gemini Details turns it into a stated intention. Kobi also said he would reuse 80-90% of the client's ERD (line 451).

notes: Project kickoff (meeting_type 'other': kickoff). No Jira keys were said aloud. Jumpr presented the plan as tentative placeholders and said 'everything is negotiable' (lines 275, 413), so most Jumpr plan items are marked 'proposed' unless the client explicitly accepted them. In the transcript, Waleed (line 166) puts payouts in the second phase, but Kobi's PRD breakdown (line 428) puts payouts in Phase 3; this is unresolved. Gemini Details was also checked against the transcript as part of the Gemini summary. Rule 5: skipped a personnel joke about firing staff (lines 128, 219), time-and-materials/billing remarks (line 471), the weekly hours-consumption report and budget remarks (lines 428, 622), and personal remarks about the client admin (lines 743-748). Quotes are verbatim substrings of the transcript lines; a multi-line quote joins segments with ' / ' and may skip lines in between. ASR: Kobe=Kobi, sauna=Asana, parody=PRD, Fart flags=fraud flags, Straw=Strahinja, Jester=Jumpr implementation lead (name as heard).
